image_description: A close-up photograph of a brown butterfly, identified as a ringlet (Aphantopus hyperantus), resting on a green leaf. The wings are held closed, displaying the ventral side which is uniformly brown with distinct rows of small eyespots (ocelli) featuring white centers and black rings. The body is slender, hairy, and brown. One clubbed antenna is clearly visible. The background consists of blurred green foliage.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The right antenna is clearly visible and exhibits the characteristic thickened tip (club) of a butterfly.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The wing coloration is uniform brown, and multiple ocelli are clearly arranged in a row along the hindwing margin.

The body appears slender relative to the wings and has a visible fuzzy/hairy texture.

custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the symmetry of the eyespots (ocelli). AI generators often distort these circular patterns into ovals or merge them. Verify if the 'brush-like' forelegs are plausibly hidden or if their absence suggests a generation error. Check for any 'haloing' around the wing edges against the green background.
